pr_title: [WIP] add a remove subcommand to `ansible-galaxy collection`
pr_body:
##### SUMMARY
Adds a 'remove' subcommand to `ansible-galaxy collection` to delete the directories of installed collections and dependencies

Currently this deletes matching collections from all search paths - should that be optional/not the default?

Fixes #67759

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Feature Pull Request

Thanks for the feedback @jborean93.

In addition to your points, I was wondering what the behavior should be when something other than a collection name is provided (like a path to a tar.gz file). I think it would be really convenient if a requirements.yml file could be used for installing and removing collections. `verify` requires a collection name because the collection is compared to the one on a galaxy server, but I think in this case we could probably just use the collection source to find the collection name and then delete it if it's installed. What do you think? We could also maybe limit the scope of this and add support for a requirements.yml file later...

```
Multiple collections found
    Will be prompted for confirmation of which one(s) to remove (or a for all)
    Should it fail or require a further confirmation argument like --force
```
I really don't like interactive prompting. I toyed with an `--all` flag. I'm not really sure in what situations someone would *want* different versions of collections installed to multiple paths in the collections paths at the same time (since `ansible-galaxy install` tries not to do that it seems like it would have to be pretty intentional). I really like that `ansible-galaxy collection list` shows all paths a collection is in though, and it would be nice if removal worked in tandem.
```
Ignoring failures
    Should we ignore if asked or consider a failure a failure
```
I followed the --ignore-errors pattern from other options, but I'm also fine with removing it. The only case I'd be worried about is if a `requirements.yml` is supported, and there's no way to skip errors, I'd definitely want removing collections installed from tar.gz and git repo sources to also work.
```
...
    How do we deal with deps for other collections
```
I agree with your review comment. We should probably process everything up front and not remove deps that are being used by other collections. Should that be an error?
```
...
    Should we have a clean option to remove any orphaned deps
```
How would you know if it's an orphaned dep or standalone collection?

This feature would be great: I'm trying to prune unused collections in order to reduce a Docker image built on Ansible. A lot of data resides in the ansible_collections folder and removing using ansible-galaxy would be a very useful feature. Can I do something to help?

> Can I do something to help?

This needs to be rebased/remade now that we've replaced the dependency resolver completely so it'll take some time to get done. We still have some time before the feature freeze, though.
OK I'll take a look this evening, see if I can contribute or if it's beyond my capabilities

I think it's clear enough for me to wrap my head around. The question is from where I can take things to contribute. I can start by forking & branching ansible:devel and see if I can reconcile the commits by @s-hertel with the changes in the code base. I could open a new PR then, referencing this on. Would this be workable?

@reinvantveer Thanks for the interest! This needs to be reworked from scratch to fit naturally with the changes made in 595413d11346b6f26bb3d9df2d8e05f2747508a3. Trying to salvage the commits here is not worth the effort. Finishing `--upgrade`/explicit upgrades is the immediate priority (https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/73336) and then I plan to open a new PR to address #67759.

@reinvantveer I just wanted to add that this improvement is on our roadmap as a part of our effort to improve the `ansible-galaxy collection` subcommands UX for ansible-core v2.12 (https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/devel/roadmap/ROADMAP_2_11.html). That PR Sloane mentioned was a colossal refactoring replacing the old in-house way of resolving collection dependencies.

That said if you want to cheap in, feel free to go ahead and submit a PR. Yes, you'd need to branch out of `ansible:devel`, and maybe the tests added in this PR would be useful, so you may want to add Sloane's fork as a Git remote and cherry-pick those. Keep in mind, however, that we want this done before the feature freeze on Feb 12 so we may have to hake over and extend/polish your work at some point.

You may open a pull request marked as a `Draft` and get regular feedback while working on it, this will help us see how ready the patch is and help you out if you have any questions.

P.S. If you feel like it's too much, just make sure to tell us to pick it up before it's too late. Have fun :)
P.P.S. Oh, and you may look at https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/devel/community/ / https://docs.ansible.com/ansible/devel/community/development_process.html#making-your-pr-merge-worthy for some contributing guidance + there's an `#ansible-devel` channel on Freenode IRC, come by to chat if you need any help.
OK, Feb 12 I'd certainly not make that, but thanks!

@reinvantveer (/anyone else following this PR) - Just to clarify, it was discussed as a feature for 2.11 and would have needed to be done by the Feb 12th deadline, but it was not an official part of the roadmap linked above (more of a stretch goal). We've decided against trying to rush it into 2.11 at this point so it can be more thoughtfully planned out, but I've created another draft on top of the dep resolver changes here: #73464.

issue_context.title: Add ansible-galaxy collection uninstall
issue_context.body:
##### SUMMARY
While users can just delete the directory it would be nice to have a command that removed/uninstalled collections in the current (or all found paths) and it's dependencies using and `ansible-galaxy` command.

##### ISSUE TYPE
- Feature Idea

##### COMPONENT NAME
ansible-galaxy
comments:

* [`lib/ansible/galaxy`](https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/lib/ansible/galaxy)

If these files are inaccurate, please update the `component name` section of the description or use the `!component` bot command.

[click here for bot help](https://github.com/ansible/ansibullbot/blob/master/ISSUE_HELP.md)

This would be nice to have just to make the galaxy cli more 'feature complete', as every other dependency management tool I've used has a similar "remove dependency" feature (most also edit the default dependency listing file (e.g. remove it from `requirements.yml`) but that would probably be out of scope here.

Its particularly confusing when contributing to module development because I currently have three versions of the same module:

 - 2.9
 - collection installed in the venv
 - git checkout
It would be great to have it!

I vote for that. 
Had a scenario i forgot to set collections_paths in ansible.cfg (usually ./collections inside my ansible-book with alternate directory layout) and after sharing my mates moant because the collection was missing.
Thus I also wanted to cleanup my userspace after moving the collection(s) and this lead me to this issue I now encourage to add this "feature".

still not there 

ansible-galaxy  collection -h
usage: ansible-galaxy collection [-h] COLLECTION_ACTION ...

positional arguments:
  COLLECTION_ACTION
    init             Initialize new collection with the base structure of a collection.
    build            Build an Ansible collection artifact that can be publish to Ansible Galaxy.
    publish          Publish a collection artifact to Ansible Galaxy.
    install          Install collection(s) from file(s), URL(s) or Ansible Galaxy

optional arguments:
  -h, --help         show this help message and exit
This issue will be closed once it has been implemented. So far there have been attempts but nothing concrete is in place yet.

As a workaround until this is implemented, to uninstall i.e. one copy `community.general` what I ran is:

    rm -rf ~/.ansible/collections/ansible_collections/community/general
    rm -rf ./venv/lib/python3.9/site-packages/ansible_collections/community/general

(Based on thumbs-up emoji reactions, it looks like this helped other people too!)

> rm -rf ~/.ansible/collections/ansible_collections/community/general

@darthwalsh I've tried this one and its seems working just fine.

https://github.com/bcoca/std/blob/devel/list_collections.py <= for those using older ansible to list collections (does not show dupes)
https://github.com/bcoca/std/blob/devel/get_collection_info.py <= get info from a collection (also does not see dupes)

both give you the install path so easy to pass to `|rm -rf`
That would be great, I vote for that also.

plus 1

This would be super handy.
Is anyone still working on this?

I've run into an issue where I now have two versions of the same collection, creating a fatal conflict.

So I would certainly say that this is a necessary feature, if there is a non-zero chance that `ansible-galaxy` will install conflicting dependencies it doesn't know what to do with....
@stainer how is the conflict 'fatal'? every run should use precedence (first found) and ignore the 2nd installation.
I vote for this

> https://github.com/bcoca/std/blob/devel/list_collections.py <= for those using older ansible to list collections (does not show dupes) https://github.com/bcoca/std/blob/devel/get_collection_info.py <= get info from a collection (also does not see dupes)
> 
> both give you the install path so easy to pass to `|rm -rf`

nice hack, but seems that's might not be enough.

experimenting with local Galaxy server I've found out that `ansible-galaxy install -s <server>` does drops `<namespace>.<collection>-<version>.info` folder alongside with ordinary `<namespace>/<collection>` folder:

```shell
% ls -lna  ~/.ansible/collections/ansible_collections/                                                        
total 0
drwxr-xr-x  5 501  20  160 Jul 12 15:40 .
drwxr-xr-x  3 501  20   96 Apr  7 11:30 ..
drwxr-xr-x  3 501  20   96 Jul 12 15:40 newswangerd
drwxr-xr-x  3 501  20   96 Jul 12 15:40 newswangerd.the_collectionizer-2.0.1.info
```

the `newswangerd` here is an example collection https://galaxy.ansible.com/newswangerd/collection_demo that was installed from  local AG server like this:

```shell
% ansible-galaxy --version                                                                                 
ansible-galaxy [core 2.15.1]
...
% ansible-galaxy collection install  -s http://localhost:5000/api newswangerd.the_collectionizer 
...
```

The contents of that folder is some meta about collection download source.
```shell
% cat  ~/.ansible/collections/ansible_collections/newswangerd.the_collectionizer-2.0.1.info/GALAXY.YML                                                       

download_url: http://localhost:5000/artifacts/newswangerd-the_collectionizer-2.0.1.tar.gz
format_version: 1.0.0
name: the_collectionizer
namespace: newswangerd
server: http://localhost:5000/api
signatures:
- signature: '-----BEGIN PGP SIGNATURE-----
   ...
    -----END PGP SIGNATURE-----
    '
version: 2.0.1
version_url: http://localhost:5000/api/v3/collections/newswangerd/the_collectionizer/versions/2.0.1/
```

So, I guess to clean up fully, those `<...>.info` folders should be removed as well.

I managed to install two different versions of a collection and I only know where 1 of those resides and that is mostly because of the above comments in this issue. Not a great user experience so far to be honest.

_example:_ remove previously installed ansible collections

~~~shell
rm -rf -- ~/.ansible/{galaxy_token,collections}
~~~
_(prefix may vary; test sample is user vagrant on generic/ubuntu2004 with ansible 2.9.6)_

review_comments: Not in my opinion. I would like `ansible-galaxy collection remove` to work with a requirements.yml (using the same file to install, update, and remove collections is very convenient when there are a lot of them) and my `--ignore-errors` got a -1. Other suggestions of how to be usable with a requirements.yml are welcome.

Well, then it needs a better logic to retrieve metadata from the concrete artifact pointers like URL/SCM (the tmp artifacts manager I'm working on should help with that). And also `len(req_name.split('.')) != 2` is a different class of an error. If an entry is clearly an invalid identifier, it shouldn't be silently ignored.

Also, if I'm reading this correctly, the message "skipping this" is printed but there's no actual skip (`continue`?) in code.

I could download the tar.gz/git SCM, and parse the name from that to see if it's installed. If we do that, I think `verify` and upgrading a collection should probably work the same way.

Edit: Oops, responded before I refreshed to see your response above.

Btw- `len(req_name.split('.')) != 2` is less intended to validate the collection name, than identify things that are not collection names. Checking it's a valid collection identifier is not what this was intended to do, though we could add that (but this didn't really seem like the right place - better in the dep resolver maybe).
Yes, since I'm working on a standardized way to do this already, you probably shouldn't spend effort on implementing this.

What's the behaviour when you have a requirements file of and a different version of that collection is installed

```yaml
collections:
- name: community.general
  version: 1.0.0
```

Looking through the code it seems like it will skip this collection due to [this check](https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/71800/files#diff-2de3c8cc3e7fae814d02b3058f0c8f9eR621). Is that the desired behaviour or should we be removing all the collections specified regardless of the version in a requirements file?

That is intentional. Using that requirements file to remove a collection would be equivalent to `ansible-galaxy collection remove community.general:1.0.0` or `ansible-galaxy collection remove community.general:==1.0.0`; if a version other than 1.0.0 is installed, it won't be removed. Does that seem like surprising behavior?
@s-hertel did we talk about `remove` vs `uninstall`? It occurred to me that people switching from pip may expect `uninstall`.
To be honest this was the first thing I tried before finding out that this wasn't something in ansible-galaxy yet
